newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firm after the Conf futures contract surged late in the day. German Bunds also gained late, helped by regional German inflation data.
One trader expected sharp price gains which would hurt what he thought were a large number of shorts held in Swiss bonds.
"It is boring but dangerous on the upside," he said.

He said further gains in the Swiss franc may lead to curve steepening if it had the expected impact of bringing Swiss short-term interest rates lower. Latest remarks on Swiss monetary policy were expected late Tuesday when Swiss National Bank vice-chairman Jean-Pierre Roth is due to speak in Geneva.
Roth's speech was due to start at 1630 GMT.
French president Jacques Chirac's call for an early French parliamentary election on Monday, meanwhile, may support the Swiss franc, traders said.
Chirac said his decision, announced Monday, was aimed at giving French people a chance to "express themselves clearly on the scale and speed of change over the next five years."
In the market, the decision led to doubts about the future of France's commitment to Economic and Monetary Union. Such uncertainty was also seen likely to benefit the Swiss franc, one trader said.
Comi medium-term bond up five at 111.05
Euro Swiss francs up two at 98.09.
